data.title: Cascader
data.tagline: Choose a path one level at a time
data.description: A cascader works for data such as country, state, and city or a nested product category. Keep the current path visible and explain whether a parent level can be selected. If users need items from several branches at once, a tree selector is usually clearer.

use: Any choice that follows one hierarchy path
avoid: Use it for data with no real parent-child relationship
Hide the chosen path after the panel closes
Use several steps when each level has only a few options

lessonPractice.title: A shipping address must choose one final region through state, city, and district and let the user confirm the full path. Which approach fits?

options.label: Use a cascader to choose one path level by level, show the full path afterward, and submit the leaf-region ID
options.feedback: Correct. The task needs one parent-child path, and a cascader preserves both the sequence and final result.

options.label: Use a multi-select tree, choose several states and cities, and treat a partial parent as the address result
options.feedback: A multi-select tree fits several scopes across branches, not one final shipping region.

options.label: Use three unrelated dropdowns and let people combine any state, city, and district
options.feedback: Independent choices cannot preserve the hierarchy and may submit a region combination that does not exist.

data.agentPrompt: Change the shipping-region field to a province → city → district cascader that selects one path at a time, without allowing a parent to become the final result. Show the full path after the panel closes, submit the leaf-region ID, and support full-path search when the option set is large. Test the initial state, level-by-level selection, changing an earlier level, search, and form submission, and confirm the displayed path matches the submitted value.
